opportunities_ranked.name: ForecastEx (IBKR) Incentive Coupon -- Rule 612, collateral yield
opportunities_ranked.venue: ForecastEx LLC (CFTC-registered DCM+DCO, wholly owned IBKR subsidiary)

opportunities_ranked.us_person_status: US-LEGAL, no geo-block. This is IBKR's own regulated US product; an ordinary IBKR brokerage account is the only prerequisite (same conclusion venue_expansion/out/venues_us.json already reached for market access generally).

mechanics.primary_source: venue_expansion/cache/fx_rulebook.pdf, ForecastEx LLC Rulebook Rule 612 'Investment of Member Funds', p.54 -- parsed directly with pypdf in this task (not previously mined for this rule; S3_FORECASTEX.md and FINDINGS.md only referenced the coupon qualitatively).
mechanics.exact_formula_DOCUMENTED: Rule 612(c)(3): 'Coupon Rate = (EFFR - 50 basis points) / 2', where EFFR is the Effective Federal Funds Rate published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Rule 612(c)(5): the minimum monthly coupon accruing to Customers 'can never be less than zero' -- a floor, not a ceiling; Rule 612(c)(2) states the Clearinghouse-to-FCM coupon is 'equal to or greater than' this floor, i.e. FCM Members (IBKR) may pass through more than the formula's minimum at their discretion.
mechanics.accrual_base: Rule 612(c)(1): 'Customer positions in Customer Collateral Accounts will accrue monthly coupons based on the daily settlement value of each Customer's positions' -- i.e. paid on held collateral backing open positions (and, per secondary IBKR marketing pages, cash collateral generally), same accrual-on-holdings shape as Kalshi's APY program (rev_kalshi_programs.json rank 1).
mechanics.payment_frequency: Accrues daily, paid monthly (Rule 612(c) header language + corroborated by every secondary IBKR source found).
mechanics.current_EFFR: 3.63% as of 2026-07-27 (Federal Reserve H.15 release / NY Fed EFFR series, via WebSearch -- DOCUMENTED, dated).
mechanics.computed_minimum_coupon: (3.63% - 0.50%) / 2 = 1.565% APY -- this is the RULEBOOK FLOOR, an ESTIMATE computed from a DOCUMENTED formula plus a DOCUMENTED current EFFR, not itself a quoted rate.
mechanics.reported_actual_rate_UNVERIFIED: Secondary sources (WebSearch, no single page fetched cleanly -- ibkrguides.com 403'd this container) report inconsistent current figures: 3.13% APY ('IBKR US platform'), 3.80% APY (pm.wiki), 4.83% APR (an ibkrguides.com page summary). These likely reflect different snapshot dates as EFFR has moved, and/or IBKR passing through more than the Rule 612 floor per its (c)(2) discretion -- none independently confirmed live in this task (the two direct-fetch attempts at ibkrguides.com and interactivebrokers.com/campus both returned HTTP 403 to this container). Treat 1.565% as the defensible DOCUMENTED-formula floor and ~3-4% as a plausible but UNVERIFIED actual-paid range; before sizing, pull the rate directly from an authenticated IBKR account view.
mechanics.comparison_to_kalshi: ForecastEx's rulebook FLOOR (1.565% at today's EFFR) is materially below Kalshi's documented actual 3.25% (rev_kalshi_programs.json rank 1). If the UNVERIFIED ~3.13-3.80% actual-paid figures hold up, ForecastEx is roughly at parity with Kalshi; this needs live confirmation before choosing where to park idle/margin capital across the two venues.

opportunities_ranked.us_person_status: NON-DEPLOYABLE FOR THIS OPERATOR. Stated plainly, no hedging: Polymarket's global venue is geo-blocked to US persons per its 2022 CFTC settlement (ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md section 6, reconfirmed there as of 2026-07-19). The Maker Rebates program runs on this exact venue's fee/CLOB infrastructure -- it pays out in 'pUSD', the global venue's own settlement currency, per docs.polymarket.com, which is not a Polymarket US (QCX) concept anywhere found. venues_us.json (2026-07-23) separately confirmed Polymarket US does not list weather markets at all and gates its API behind an institutional application process -- so even if this rebate program had a Polymarket US analog (not established), the weather category it was asked about specifically would not exist there. This is a dead end on access grounds alone; the mechanics below are documented for completeness, not because they are actionable.

mechanics.citation_rebateRate_live_value: venue_expansion/ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md line 132 (this repo's own live-pulled data, 2026-07-19): every sampled Weather-category market's `feeSchedule` field reads `{"exponent": 1, "rate": 0.05, "takerOnly": true, "rebateRate": 0.25}` -- DOCUMENTED, first-party, already on disk.
mechanics.citation_program_pages: https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/maker-rebates.md and https://docs.polymarket.com/llms.txt index (live WebFetch, 2026-07-30) -- confirms this is a DISTINCT program from Liquidity Rewards (rank 4 below), paying in 'pUSD'.
mechanics.what_rebateRate_0.25_means: 25% of the TAKER FEES collected in a given category (here: Weather) are pooled and redistributed daily to that day's makers, pro-rata by each maker's fee-equivalent contribution: rebate = (your_fee_equivalent / total_fee_equivalent_that_day_in_category) x rebate_pool, where fee_equivalent for a fill = C x feeRate x p x (1-p) (the same taker-fee formula pmkt_final_verdict.md already used, feeRate=0.05 for weather). It is NOT a fixed rebate per contract -- it is a share of a pool sized by how much taker fee volume the whole category generated that day, so a maker's payout depends on category-wide taker activity, not just the maker's own volume.
mechanics.per_category_rates_cross-checked: WebSearch-synthesized secondary read of docs.polymarket.com content: Crypto 20%, Sports 15%, Finance/Politics/Economics/Culture/Weather/Tech/Mentions/Other 25% each, Geopolitics fee-free (no rebate pool exists there). Weather's 25% matches the live-pulled 0.25 in pmkt_final_verdict.md exactly -- corroborated two ways.
mechanics.payout_mechanics: Distributed daily; minimum $1 pUSD threshold to trigger a payout (sub-$1 days do not pay and do not appear to roll over, per docs), same shape as the separate Liquidity Rewards program's $1 floor.

cost_model.instruction: This requires GETTING FILLED as a maker, so MAKER_VIABILITY.md's bounds are the applicable cost model per orchestrator instruction -- but this is now moot given the access verdict above; not worked further.
cost_model.moot_reason: Zero achievable revenue for a US-person operator regardless of the fill-cost arithmetic, because the venue itself cannot be reached.

opportunities_ranked.name: Polymarket Liquidity Rewards Program
opportunities_ranked.venue: Polymarket GLOBAL (same geo-blocked venue as rank 3, same non-deployability verdict, restated per-item as instructed, not soft-pedaled)
opportunities_ranked.type: CONTRACTUAL INCENTIVE POOL -- quoting-PRESENCE weighted, no fill required (the Polymarket analog of Kalshi's LIP, rev_kalshi_programs.json rank 2)
opportunities_ranked.us_person_status: NON-DEPLOYABLE FOR THIS OPERATOR -- identical reasoning to rank 3: this is the global venue's program (docs.polymarket.com/market-makers/liquidity-rewards), geo-blocked to US persons; Polymarket US does not list weather and gates its API. Stated plainly.

mechanics.citation: https://docs.polymarket.com/market-makers/liquidity-rewards (live WebFetch, 2026-07-30, DOCUMENTED) + corroborating WebSearch triangulation (help.polymarket.com, startpolymarket.com, bravadotrade.com).
mechanics.scoring_formula: S(v,s) = ((v-s)/v)^2 x b, where v = the market's maximum qualifying spread and s = the order's actual spread from the 'size-cutoff-adjusted midpoint' -- a quadratic decay that 'heavily penalizes' resting orders away from the midpoint, order SIZE multiplies this score, and per-maker scores are aggregated per side then normalized against the sum of all makers' scores that epoch: your_share = your_Q_epoch / sum(all_makers_Q_epoch), reward = your_share x market's_reward_allocation.
mechanics.two_sided_requirement: When the midpoint sits in [0.10, 0.90], quoting only one side divides your score by 3.0 (a real but survivable penalty); outside that range liquidity must be double-sided to score at all.
mechanics.eligibility: Automatic for any resting limit order in an incentivized market -- no application/approval gate (matches Kalshi LIP's shape, unlike the Kalshi/ForecastEx MM-agreement programs). Each incentivized market separately configures its own minimum qualifying order size, maximum qualifying spread, and reward allocation.
mechanics.payout: Daily at midnight UTC, $1 minimum threshold (sub-$1 days do not pay).
mechanics.why_this_stack_would_fit_if_deployable: This is structurally the SAME match this repo already identified for Kalshi's LIP (rev_kalshi_programs.json rank 2): it pays for verified resting-order presence and proximity, not fill P&L -- exactly the axis ENGINEERING_STACK.md's warm-path/persistent-WS/queue-position tooling is built for, and explicitly does NOT require winning fills the way the killed statistical-edge studies needed to.

cost_model.instruction: No quoting-obligation fill-cost applies to the SCORE itself (resting orders that never fill still earn reward share) -- the only fill-cost exposure is incidental, from orders placed close enough to the midpoint to score well also being more likely to get run over. This is the one line item in the whole cross-venue sweep that would have used MAKER_VIABILITY's bounds as a genuine incidental-fill-risk overlay rather than a core cost, exactly like Kalshi LIP -- but it is moot here for the same access reason as rank 3.

opportunities_ranked.verdict: The single best-matched payout mechanism to the verified engineering stack found anywhere in this entire cross-venue sweep (presence-rewarded, not fill-rewarded, no relationship gate) -- and it is completely inaccessible to a US-person operator. This is the sharpest illustration in the file of the geo-block cost: the one program that would have been a near-frictionless fit for the built infrastructure is the one program this operator cannot legally touch on this venue.

top_recommendation.summary: One clean, immediately-capturable item and one promising-but-unresolved item survive from this cross-venue sweep; two well-matched programs are confirmed dead on access grounds and should be crossed off decisively rather than revisited. (1) ForecastEx's Rule 612 incentive coupon is the cross-venue twin of Kalshi's APY finding: DOCUMENTED formula (Coupon Rate = (EFFR-50bps)/2, floor zero), computes to a 1.565% APY rulebook MINIMUM at today's 3.63% EFFR, with UNVERIFIED secondary reports of ~3.13-3.80% actually being paid -- zero quoting obligation, capturable on whatever collateral the program already holds at ForecastEx, confirm the live rate in 5 minutes via account view before finalizing sizing alongside Kalshi's 3.25%. (2) ProphetX's Liquidity Rewards Program is a real $2k/day-scale-per-category, US-legal, sports-only pool, but this task could not resolve (both source pages 403'd) whether it rewards resting presence (free, like Kalshi LIP / Polymarket Liquidity Rewards) or filled maker volume (fill-cost-exposed, like a rebate) -- that single fact determines whether it belongs next to item (1) or gets killed by the same adverse-selection logic that killed the Kalshi maker study; resolve with one direct account-authenticated page view before any capital commitment. On the access side: Polymarket's Maker Rebates (rebateRate 0.25 on Weather = 25% of category taker fees, pooled and distributed pro-rata daily) and its separate Liquidity Rewards program (a presence-weighted quadratic-spread-scoring pool, the single best structural match to this program's engineering stack found anywhere in the sweep) are BOTH confirmed non-deployable -- Polymarket's global venue remains geo-blocked to US persons, and Polymarket US does not list weather and gates its API. State this plainly: the operator cannot reach either Polymarket program, and no amount of engineering changes that. ForecastEx's own Market Maker Program (Rule 416) is a discretionary dead end with no published economics, structurally identical to Kalshi's MM Agreement. Crypto.com's new US prediction product has no weather category and no liquidity program; Novig's Cash system is real money but not a program-terms revenue line.
